function: Learned sub-channel selection and transmit-power allocation (energy-efficiency maximization) for NOMA downlink of RSUs and UAVs; user association and UAV positioning are heuristic, not learned. p. 6, p. 8
system: NOMA downlink: RSUs and UAVs with N_A antennas (value not given), single-antenna vehicles; 2 GHz, 10 MHz, UAV altitude 30 m; no RIS. p. 4, p. 10
method: Mean-field multi-agent reinforcement learning (Nash/mean-field Q-learning), a DQN per agent with actor and critic networks of two hidden layers, 2000 training episodes. p. 8-10
data_channel: Own simulator following 3GPP TR 36.885 urban case: path loss 128.1+37.6log10(d), log-normal shadowing, Rayleigh fast fading, 2 GHz, 10 MHz; Poisson vehicle drop; no dataset. p. 10
test_conditions: Trained 2000 episodes of 100 steps; compared at 4 RSUs, 2 UAVs, 30 km/h, then sweeps of RSUs, UAVs, speed, energy, power; retraining per sweep not stated. p. 10-14
baselines: Non-learned: RAN (random power), UAO [10] (Lyapunov), SGU [3] (Stackelberg game). Learned: only own variants NUA (no UAVs) and CGM (complete game, no mean field). p. 10
metrics: Average energy efficiency (bits/Hz/J), probability of failure (unfulfilled requests or SINR below threshold), training reward curves (Fig. 3). p. 10-11
complexity: Order stated: O(n_a^(M+L)) for complete game, O(n_a^2) with mean-field, n_a the per-agent action-space size; no runtime or parameter count. p. 9-10
openness: none; own simulator, no code or data link in the paper. p. 10
q1_support: p. 10: "The simulator is generated following the evaluation methodology for the urban case defined in [24]"
q2_support: p. 10: "We train the networks for a total of 2000 episodes and set 100 steps for an episode." Missing: no statement that a trained policy is tested on a configuration, number of agents or speed not used in training; Figs. 4-9 sweep RSUs, UAVs, speed, energy and power without saying whether the agents are retrained.
q3_support: p. 10: "CGM: Complete game-based MARL method". Missing: an earlier published learned method; RAN, UAO [10] and SGU [3] are non-learned, and NUA and CGM are variants of the proposed scheme (no UAVs; no mean field).
q4_support: p. 10: "decreases to O(n_a^2) when adopting MFG"
q5_support: p. 10: "The simulator is generated following the evaluation methodology for the urban case defined in [24]." Missing: no code or data link or release statement, and no public channel dataset (own simulator).
notes: Included, area 6: the learned part is transmit-power and sub-channel allocation for RSUs and UAVs (p. 8), and learned power and resource control of aerial (UAV) links is physical layer by rule; user association (Algorithm 1, p. 7) and the UAV hovering position (p. 6) are not learned. Reviewer: confirm that UAV-assisted V2X counts as an aerial-link work of area 6, since the RSU links are terrestrial. Tables III and IV were read from the page images (p. 10, p. 11). q1 is marked met as another standardized model: the simulator follows the urban case of 3GPP TR 36.885 (reference [24], p. 14), whose channel models it names (p. 10); Table III lists path loss 128.1+37.6log10(d), log-normal shadowing and Rayleigh fading, so the reviewer should confirm that this counts and is not a custom simulator. q2: no statement of testing a trained policy on an unseen configuration; the sweeps of Figs. 4-9 do not say whether the agents are retrained. q3: no earlier published learned method is compared; NUA is the proposed scheme without UAVs and CGM is the complete-game version without the mean-field module, presented as the optimal solution (p. 10), both variants of the proposed scheme. q4: O(n_a^2) with the mean field (p. 10) against O(n_a^(M+L)) for the complete game (p. 9). q5: own simulator, no link, no public dataset. No RIS in the system (RIS appears only in reference [33], p. 15).
